situations.description: Normal operation — participants, publishers, and subscribers actively exchanging samples.
Participant shutdown or reconfiguration — Close()/close_with_drain() called while subscriptions are open.
Concurrent multi-threaded access — Send/Publish/Close invoked from different threads without external synchronisation (RELAY spec §6 req 6, 7).
Resource-constrained / overload — publish rate exceeds subscriber channel capacity (back-pressure engaged).

hazards.description: IParticipant::close() does not close previously-returned subscriber channels, so a consumer thread blocked in recv() (directly, or via dds::adapt()'s relay::INode forwarder) never observes shutdown and continues waiting on stale/absent data instead of failing over.

IPublisher::write() rejects a payload exceeding QoS.max_sample_size (ErrPayloadTooLarge), but a caller that does not check the returned std::error_code silently drops a safety-relevant command with no downstream signal.

validate_domain() only enforces the numeric range [0,232]; it cannot detect a participant joining a range-valid but semantically wrong domain, which could route data between subsystems intended to be isolated.

QoS.Deadline expiry is only reported if the caller registers with_deadline_missed(); an application that omits the callback has no signal that a sample is stale and may act on outdated data as if it were current.

A data race between concurrent Send/Publish/Close operations on the same participant/channel could corrupt in-flight samples or crash the process, violating RELAY spec §6 req 6-7 (concurrent close, concurrent sends).

safetyGoals.description: IParticipant::close() MUST close every subscriber channel already returned via new_subscriber(), unblocking any thread blocked in recv() with a defined empty/closed result.
safetyGoals.safeState: All subscriber channels report is_closed() == true and recv() returns std::nullopt within one scheduling interval of close().

safetyGoals.description: Every IPublisher::write() call site MUST propagate and act on a non-empty std::error_code (ErrPayloadTooLarge, ErrClosed, ErrTimeout) rather than assuming success.
safetyGoals.safeState: Caller observes a non-empty std::error_code and does not treat the write as delivered.

safetyGoals.description: Domain selection MUST be governed by application-level configuration review / integration testing in addition to validate_domain()'s numeric range check; cpp-DDS documents this residual risk rather than silently assuming isolation.
safetyGoals.safeState: Deployment configuration is reviewed so that isolated subsystems are assigned disjoint domains; documented in README / integration checklist.

safetyGoals.description: Applications with a freshness requirement MUST register with_deadline_missed() on every subscriber that carries safety-relevant data.
safetyGoals.safeState: The deadline_missed callback fires and the application discards or flags the stale sample before acting on it.

safetyGoals.description: All shared participant/channel state MUST remain race-free under concurrent Send/Publish/Close per RELAY spec §6 req 6-7, verified continuously by the ASan+UBSan CI gate (.github/workflows/ci.yml `sanitizers` job) and the concurrency test suite (REQ-SAFETY-001).
safetyGoals.safeState: No data race reported by ThreadSanitizer/ASan+UBSan across the concurrent test suite; process does not crash or corrupt in-flight samples.
